html:
Wankarani was a culture of the high plateau, the altiplano, of Bolivia, north of Lake Poopó near Oruro. Its dates are uncertain, roughly from the second millennium BCE into the first centuries CE.

Its people lived in villages of round adobe houses, often on mounds that built up over generations. They herded llamas and grew potatoes and quinoa at about 3,700 m. They carved stone heads of llamas, perhaps for rituals, and were among the early metalworkers of the Andes, working copper.

It was one of the first settled farming and herding societies of the altiplano, along with the Chiripa culture near Lake Titicaca, and came before the rise of Tiwanaku. Hunters of the open highlands, the Andean hunter-gatherers, lived around them.
